# The taxonomy {#taxonomy-overview}

The Kailash catalogue is organised into four named tool layers (plus a
CORE substrate that hosts none of them), and within each layer into
numbered categories. The catalogue of record is **the tool manifest** —
a single hand-maintained registry in the packages repository; packaging,
menus, CLI and the generated docs all derive from it.

Tool counts below are the census at this guide's build (337 rows across
32 categories; [the manifest](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-packages/tree/main/manifest)
always carries the live numbers).

## Layer CLASSIC (c-01 … c-10) — 147 tools

Software-only heritage security foundation: information gathering (38),
vulnerability analysis (7), web application assessment (10), database
assessment (7), password & offline-credential attacks (16), reverse
engineering (26), Signal & SDR — the opt-in carve-out (6), exploitation
& post-exploitation, software-only (9), forensics/IR & reporting (21),
runtime AppSec for AI systems (7).

## Layer ATTACK (a-01 … a-08) — 58 tools

Offensive AI: AI reconnaissance & target discovery (5), LLM prompt
injection & jailbreaking (8), agentic/MCP/tool-use attacks (9), model
supply chain & artefact poisoning (8), model extraction/inversion &
membership inference (8), multi-modal & physical-AI attacks (5), AI
system exploitation (9), data poisoning & dataset attacks (6).

## Layer DEFENCE (d-01 … d-07) — 45 tools

Defensive AI & assurance: runtime defence & guardrails (7), detection/
monitoring/observability & IR (8), assurance/evals/benchmarks (6),
model provenance/signing/trust (10), AI threat modelling (6),
governance & regulation mapping (4), standards verification (4).

## Layer OPS (o-01 … o-07) — 87 tools

The platform: MLOps & ML engineering (18), compute & serving
infrastructure (11), vector stores & retrieval (9), local LLM &
inference labs (5), AI engineering SDKs & dev environment (26),
documentation/reporting/authoring (10), agent & MCP operability (8).

## How the navigation works

Categories are the navigation system on every surface: the desktop
menu, the `kailash` CLI's listing, per-category docs, and this guide's
reference part all use the same vocabulary — three views over one
manifest. A tool lands exactly once, with one primary category and
secondary cross-references only where dual-use is real.
